rows.text: Agents, conversations, connectors and memories stay in this workspace. Claude Code and OpenCode sign-ins are still shared on this computer. A workspace is not an OS sandbox.
The app’s language, and the one the agents reply in.
Goes into every conversation of every agent: who you are, what you do, what matters now and what never to do.
How Tucano looks to you. It changes only for you.
System follows the computer’s light and dark through the day.
The chirp when an agent needs you and when it’s done. Off, notifications still show up, silently.
Sends a notification now, to see that it comes.

Speak instead of typing: click the microphone in the message field, or ⌥ Space on a Mac and Ctrl+Space elsewhere, and click again to finish. The audio becomes text on this Tucano's server, through no other service. On a server, the Light model is much faster. The text stays in the field for you to review before sending.
Opens the list of what the agent is doing under its reply. Off, only the line with what it’s doing now stays; a click on it opens the steps. It changes only for you.
Now and then, a quiet line at the foot of the sidebar with a quick question. For that, Tucano checks tucano.sh a few times a day. It sends nothing of yours.
A bug, an idea, anything. Also in "Send feedback", at the foot of the sidebar.

For every agent: how far they go on their own and what asks for your approval first, with a button in the conversation. On each agent’s page you can change it for that agent only. Reading and looking into things never asks.

An email, a page or an issue can carry instructions someone else wrote. With this on, after reading something like that, sending, publishing, paying, deleting and risky clicks ask for your approval, even where a rule lets it do them alone.

When it hits it, the agent pauses. If it was getting somewhere it goes on by itself (see Keep going on its own, below); if not, you decide whether it continues. For an agent with no monthly limit, it is taken over 10 million tokens.
No text and no tool finishing. Long work that’s moving isn’t cut off.

When a reply reaches its limit while it was getting somewhere, the agent goes on by itself up to 10 times in a row before waiting for you. A reply cut because the app closed goes on when it opens again. The monthly limit still holds.
Routines run while the app is open, even with the window closed.
So no routine depends on you remembering to open the app.
Routines and triggers wait and run when it ends (as late ones). What you send still gets answered.
What Tuca changes inside the app: agents, teams, channels and routines.

What he proposes goes in as soon as he finishes replying, and the card gets an Undo for 24 hours. Connector access and the monthly limit still wait for you to confirm. Off, everything waits for you to click Apply.
How the app finds what the agent asks to click (“the Search button”). By text it’s free and handles most cases; when it can’t find it, the agent uses the element’s number.
Change each agent’s model or apply one to several at once. Applies to future replies; replies already running continue as they are.
Switching harnesses uses the default login. The fallback model stays the same.
Bulk changes include selected agents outside the search. Archived agents are included only when the option above is checked.

Where the agents run: an endpoint of yours, with nothing to install, or a program the way you set it up (on your plan, your company’s gateway or your providers). Tucano never sees or stores the programs’ credentials; an endpoint’s key is kept here, encrypted.

More than one Claude Code, Codex or Antigravity login, like a work account and a personal one. Each agent picks its account on its page. You sign in through the CLI itself: Tucano never sees or stores the password.
A small model that reads the conversation and decides who replies in channels. It grants no permissions at all.
Go for a fast model: it runs before every reply in a channel.
A small model summarizes what leaves each conversation’s window and, from the same stretch, picks what’s worth remembering about you.
Runs every ~20 messages in a long conversation.
Only what you said counts, never what an agent assumed.
Approvals with buttons, the agents’ questions (just reply to the message) and routine results, in your Telegram. Handy for a routine that asks for approval in the middle of the night.
Telegram receives the text of approvals and questions (tool, arguments, reason) and the routines’ replies. The token stays in the system’s vault. A high-risk action takes two taps.

Connect your harness (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode…) to this Tucano. From there it understands the team, talks to the agents and sets up agents, channels, routines and skills, as you would here.
One key per harness. It acts as you, with what you can do here, up to the level you pick.
The harness and where it runs: “Claude Code on the laptop”.
Also creates and changes agents, channels, routines, skills, connectors and memories.
The agents read this to know who they talk to.
Use Tucano on an iPhone with your account here: your DMs, your approvals and the questions agents ask you.
Who has access to this Tucano and what each person can do. Each person’s DMs stay private.
Who did what in this Tucano. What’s said in DMs never shows here.

The team in a .md file (agents, skills, channels and routines, without credentials or conversations), to keep or take to another computer. Agents from OpenBot, Grok Bot and Hermes come in too, with no connector and web search off.

Bringing the Tucano from your computer? In the desktop app, use Export everything (Settings › General) and send the file here: agents, conversations, memories, wiki and files replace this Tucano's. A daily backup (.db, from the backups folder) works too, with the database only.
You’re on version 0.2.44. Updates work in the installed app.
Save decisions, facts, and results to wiki pages. Disable per channel or DM in its menu.
New pages save immediately. Automatic also applies pending edits. Undo from History.
Find conflicts, outdated facts, and duplicates in Care.
Markdown files, compatible with Obsidian, iCloud, and Git.
Use a repository as your wiki. Changes sync both ways.
Upload a zipped vault to copy its notes, folders, links, and attachments.
Page types and writing rules for agents and the curator.
